chunks: And from him, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Mushma’al Bin Sa’ad, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) regarding
a man who left five brothers and a grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from six (shares), for every one among them, a share'.
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided when a man leaves five brothers and a grandfather?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'Tasib' (residual inheritance) where the paternal grandfather does not exclude the full brothers, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence compared to some Sunni schools. The division into six shares reflects the specific legal status of the grandfather as a primary heir alongside the siblings, emphasizing the equity of distribution among close male kin. This ruling underscores the Imam's authority in clarifying complex inheritance scenarios that are not explicitly detailed in the Quranic verses.
